description.narrative:
FOTEA provides photographic and visual literacy education and organises competitions, exhibitions, and other lens-based media-related activities. FOTEA’s vision is to make photography and photographic education accessible to everyone, to ensure that citizens havethe rights and tools to tell their own stories, and to promote the work of photographers from Uganda and East Africa nationally, regionally, and internationally.
Under the stories for change project, FOTEA will be drawing from this experienceto mobilise young creatives between the ages of 22 and 35 in the fields of photography, videography, written word, illustration, audio and podcasting tojoin a training programme on ‘Stories 4 Change’. As part of their activities; • They will put out anopen call to ensure inclusive participation • Through a boot camp, they will train young creatives in basic photography, videography, written word, illustrations, audio, and broadcasting. • Through building blocks of story seminars, they will train youngcreatives in in-depth and advanced photography, videography, written word, illustrations, audio, and broadcasting • They will Organise co-creation sessions. As a result, there will be developed creativity and technical skills of vibrant young creativesin various modes to reach optimal story quality.

participating-org.narrative:
The organisation was founded in 2016 by Anna Kućma. Back then its main purpose was to support the activities around the Uganda Press Photo Award in order to establish a financial and legal presence. It is a very small organisation and from the very beginning it has been run and managed by women. At the moment the organisation is undergoing a significant change and starting from February it will be under the new leadership of Mr Giovanni Okot.
2. ACHIEVEMENTS
FOTEA offers perhaps the most diverse and complete specialist visual education options in the East African region. We bring together young photographers and media practitioners, circumventing the established structures to engage practitioners critically, encouraging them to look beyond the boundaries of the established mediaecosystem and to develop ideas and approaches which address issues which they’re passionate about. One of our programmes, titled Photography and Visual Literacy for Active Citizenship trained more than 40 people in visual literacy and storytelling, also during COVID-19 lockdowns when many young people didn’t have much to do.
3. INSTITUTIONAL PURPOSE
FOTEA’s vision is to make photography and photographic education accessible to everyone, to ensure that citizens have the rights and tools to tell their own stories, and to promote the work of photographers from Uganda and East Africa nationally, regionally and internationally.
FOTEA’s mission is to offer a truly supportive platform for photographers in Uganda and East Africa and, through that platform, to create opportunities for people to connect, learn, and grow. FOTEA provides photographic and visual literacy education and organises competitions, exhibitions, and other lens-based media-related activities.
Institutional objectives: - Further formalise the structure of FOTEA to supporta more sustainable future for the organisation - Further expand our status as a leader for photographic <(>&<)> visual literacy education in the Eastern African Region. - Find sustainable ways of generating revenue for increased financial independence. - Standingoffice, resource centre and gallery space.
Field(s) of activity:
The organisation principally works with young people interested in photographic and video as well as broader media and art education. The organisation runs three annual awards: - Uganda Press Photo Award - East Africa Photography Award - Young Photographer Award As well as other, mainly educational activities and there includeEmerging Photographer Mentorship Programme, photo and video workshop and trainings as well as exhibitions and other cultural events. Geographically, FOTEA predominantly works in Uganda as well as in the East African Region (Ethiopia, Sudan, South Sudan, Kenya, Tanzania, Rwanda and Burundi).
4. STRATEGIC POSITIONING
Since FOTEA is based in Uganda and our work supports people working within the media and journalism landscape, our activities are often affected by political, economic and social factors. Incidences of violence or censorship, as well as the lack of any support for cultural organisations, and hostile regulations such as the recent “Film, Documentaries and Still Photography Regulations” by the Uganda Communications Commission, are ongoing threats to our production and we are conscious of these risks whenever we are planning or executing activities.
Our main sponsors, partners and collaborators: In Uganda: • Friedrich Ebert Stiftung • MoTIV • Uganda Society Library • British Council • EU Delegation to Uganda • Irish Embassy in Uganda • Makerere University, Department of Journalism and Communication, Faculty and Students • Makerere University, Margaret Trowell School of Industrial <(>&<)> Fine Arts, Faculty and Students • Other universities and learning institutions that offer media studies • Photography industry and community • 32º East, Ugandan Arts Trust Internationally: • Visura • Canon Central and North Africa • FORMAT International Photography Festival, Derby, UK • f2 International Photography Festival, Dortmund, Germany

comment.narrative: 40 young creatives (40% Female and 60% male)went through the foundational (boot camp) training and out of these, 15 creatives have gone to the advanced/indepth training level of the program (building block of story seminars and story creation) which delves into different aspects of story telling.

Due to the start date being the middle of the year, cohort 2 saw fewer quality submissions, with 80 responses. The respondents’ median age was 28 with: ● 18 - 24 = 29% ● 25 - 30 = 46% ● 31 - 40 = 25% - We had to cut down the number of boot camp participants down. 30 people were invited to participate but only 20 eventually came to the sessions with 65% of them being men and 35% women. - 15 of those were invited to return for the rest of the programme and only 12 were present for the ideation sessions - Currently, we have 8 participants, 4 women and 4 men.

During this period, the same creatives from the first sessions, January – April, are the same engaged in the ideation phase, working on their personal and group projects while collaborating with their mentors. A strategic shift occurred, enabling participants to prioritize personal projects first. This approach aimed to cultivate a sense of ownership in their storytelling journeys and foster ongoing personal and professional development. As a result, some participants were able to create something independently before they began working in groups. The number is therefore left at 0 to avoid double counting but there was work going on in this phase.

For cohort 2, there were 80 responses. The respondents’ median age was 28 with: ● 18 - 24 = 29% ● 25 - 30 = 46% ● 31 - 40 = 25% For the bootcamp, 30 people were invited to participate but only 20 eventually came to the sessions with 65% of them beingmen and 35% women. 15 of those were invited to return for the rest of the programme and only 12 were present for the ideation sessions and are now actively working on developing their stories. The gender ratio remains the same.

In total, 47 young creatives have been trained during the project. The building blocks started with 15 participants, then cohort one had 12 participants, cohort two had 8 participants, and cohort three had 12 participants, some selected from the different cohorts and others were new entrants. Specifically, the cohort 3 programme supported the development, execution and showcase of 12 projects from 12 participants. Using a unique collaborative model, the program significantly advanced participants' storytelling abilities, showcased their work and equipped them with tools to generate impactful, high-quality content across various media. The 12 participants produced work that tackled critical social issues through 4 key themes: gender and land rights; gender-based violence; disaster preparedness; shrinking civic space. A catalogue of this work was produced and is available.
Summary
-45 participants through the duration of the project 12 completed impact-driven artworks - 4 collaborative groups - A legacy exhibition with over 315 visitors during its one-week run. - An opening for the legacy exhibition with 83 attendees. - A walkthrough for the legacy
